text:
Anna K: Quick heads-up — ran a microbench suite with load-injection bursts (spikes at 2x, 5x, 10x nominal qps) and observed what looks like kernel-selection hysteresis + KV-cache miss amplification. TL;DR: p95 latency jumps when bursts land right after KV cache TTL windows expire.

Mike R: Can you paste the run command and the summary numbers?

Anna K: Sure. Ran replay-harness v2 with synthetic bursts. Command: `./harness --profile microburst --burst-mult 5 --seed 42 --kv-ttl 30s --kernel-auto`. Summary (trimmed):
```
Run: 2026-02-12 09:12 UTC
QPS baseline: 120
Burst: 600 (5x)
TTFT p95 baseline: 78ms -> during burst: 310ms
TPOT goodput: baseline 95% -> burst 61%
KV cache hit-rate: baseline 86% -> post-burst 42%
Kernel chosen: fast-fp16 -> switched to fallback-int8 under tail load
```

Sanjay P: Interesting. Two orthogonal effects: (1) kernel hysteresis — runtime keeps the previously selected kernel for a few batches before re-evaluating, (2) KV cache TTL/warmup mismatch causing many requests to miss prefix cache at the same time. Combined they amplify p95.

Eva L: Is this synthetic-only or replay too? We need apples-to-apples vs customer replay to be sure. Also how are you measuring TTFT vs TPOT here? Are you including queueing time?

Anna K: Synthetic for the initial probe. TTFT here = time from request arrival to first token emitted (includes queueing). TPOT = total prompt+output tokens/sec per GPU (goodput). I kept measurement definitions consistent across runs.

Mike R: Can you share the exact harness config snippet? We should test with two changes: (A) reduce kernel hysteresis window (evaluate kernel every batch), (B) stagger KV TTL expirations to avoid synchronized misses.

Anna K: Pasted snippet: 
```
"microburst": {
  "qps": 120,
  "burst": {"mult": 5, "duration_s": 20, "interval_s": 300},
  "kv": {"ttl_s": 30, "shard_stagger": 0},
  "kernel_selection": {"hysteresis_batches": 3, "probe_fraction": 0.03}
}
```

bench-bot: Automated run finished: 2298765432-1
Result diff: hysteresis_batches=1 -> p95 reduced 310ms -> 150ms, goodput improved 61% -> 84%. KV hit-rate still low immediately after burst (48%) but warmed faster.

Sanjay P: That suggests kernel re-eval frequency is a dominant lever. But the KV warmup pattern still matters — if many prefixes evict around same TTL, you'll get tail spikes regardless. We should add a small randomized TTL jitter shard-side.

Eva L: Agreed. For an apples-to-apples comparison vs replay we should: 1) Replay the same sequence with identical timing jitter, 2) Ensure sampling rate for p95/p99 is identical, 3) Align kernel probes/time windows. Otherwise TPOT vs QPS numbers will be misleading.

Anna K: I'll run three variants: A) probe_every_batch + staggered-kv, B) probe_every_3_batches + staggered-kv, C) probe_every_batch + no-stagger (control). Will attach raw runs.

Mike R: When you post results, include both absolute and normalized metrics (per-GPU TPOT, per-request TTFT p95/p99, and the KV-hit distribution over time). Also mark whether TTFT includes client-side enqueue delays.

Anna K: Will do. One more note: observed kernel fallback from fp16 -> int8 coincided with batch size collapse under burst tails. We should track batch composition (seq len distribution + batching depth) when correlating kernel choice with latency.

Sanjay P: Good call — add a small profiler trace for batch shapes + kernel dispatch decision. Even a 1% sampled log is enough.

bench-bot: New runs scheduled: 2298765432-A, 2298765432-B, 2298765432-C. ETA ~ 2h.

Anna K: Thanks team — I'll upload summarized CSVs and a short write-up after the runs. For now, main takeaway: kernel selection hysteresis + synchronized KV cache misses can produce >3x p95 regression during bursts; reducing hysteresis and staggering TTLs reduces the effect by ~50-70% in our early tests. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
